note: Clues never contain the answer. Short forms that a player would reasonably type are listed in `accept`; the trainer also accepts the surname automatically where the name has no lowercase particle. Answers are matched case- and accent-insensitively, so Beyonce and Pele are accepted for Beyoncé and Pelé.

people.name: Freddie Mercury
people.clue: Lead singer of Queen, famous for the six-minute operatic epic Bohemian Rhapsody.

people.name: Elvis Presley
people.clue: American singer crowned the King of Rock and Roll, known for Jailhouse Rock and a Memphis mansion called Graceland.

people.name: Michael Jackson
people.clue: The King of Pop, whose 1982 album Thriller is the best-selling of all time, and who popularised the moonwalk.

people.name: Bob Marley
people.clue: Jamaican reggae musician behind One Love and No Woman No Cry.

people.name: Beyoncé
people.clue: American singer who rose to fame with Destiny's Child before a solo career including Single Ladies.

people.name: Taylor Swift
people.clue: American singer-songwriter who re-recorded her early albums to own the masters, and whose Eras Tour broke box-office records.

people.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
people.clue: Austrian composer and child prodigy who wrote The Magic Flute and died at 35 leaving a Requiem unfinished.

people.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
people.clue: German composer who continued writing, including the Ninth Symphony, after going deaf.

people.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
people.clue: Baroque German composer of the Brandenburg Concertos and a great many church cantatas.

people.name: John Lennon
people.clue: Beatles songwriter who later wrote Imagine and was shot outside his New York apartment in 1980.

people.name: Madonna
people.clue: American singer called the Queen of Pop, known for Like a Prayer and constant reinvention.

people.name: Aretha Franklin
people.clue: American singer known as the Queen of Soul, whose version of Respect became an anthem.

people.name: David Bowie
people.clue: English musician who invented the alter ego Ziggy Stardust and recorded Space Oddity.

people.name: Jimi Hendrix
people.clue: American guitarist famous for Purple Haze and for playing the US anthem at Woodstock.

people.name: Dolly Parton
people.clue: American country singer who wrote Jolene and I Will Always Love You, and founded a literacy charity.

people.name: Adele
people.clue: English singer whose albums are named after her age, including the one containing Rolling in the Deep.

people.name: Ed Sheeran
people.clue: English singer-songwriter who performs solo with a loop pedal, known for Shape of You.

people.name: Lady Gaga
people.clue: American singer known for Poker Face and theatrical costumes, who later won an Oscar for Shallow.

people.name: Charlie Chaplin
people.clue: Silent-film comedian who created the bowler-hatted Tramp with a cane and moustache.

people.name: Alfred Hitchcock
people.clue: English director called the Master of Suspense, behind Psycho and The Birds, who appeared briefly in his own films.

people.name: Meryl Streep
people.clue: American actor with more Academy Award nominations than anyone, known for Sophie's Choice and The Devil Wears Prada.

people.name: Steven Spielberg
people.clue: American director of Jaws, E.T. and Jurassic Park, who also made Schindler's List.

people.name: Marilyn Monroe
people.clue: American actor and 1950s icon, star of Some Like It Hot, whose white dress over a subway grate became famous.

people.name: Audrey Hepburn
people.clue: Belgian-born actor who starred in Breakfast at Tiffany's and later worked as a UNICEF ambassador.

people.name: Denzel Washington
people.clue: American actor who won Oscars for Glory and Training Day.

people.name: Quentin Tarantino
people.clue: American director of Pulp Fiction and Kill Bill, known for non-linear storytelling and long dialogue scenes.

people.name: Tom Hanks
people.clue: American actor who won back-to-back Oscars and played the title role in Forrest Gump.

people.name: Leonardo DiCaprio
people.clue: American actor who starred in Titanic and finally won an Oscar for The Revenant.

people.name: Morgan Freeman
people.clue: American actor with an instantly recognisable narrating voice, who played Red in The Shawshank Redemption.

people.name: Christopher Nolan
people.clue: British-American director of Inception and Interstellar, who won Best Director for Oppenheimer.

people.name: Viola Davis
people.clue: American actor who won an Oscar for Fences and has completed the acting Triple Crown.

people.name: Keanu Reeves
people.clue: Canadian actor who played Neo in The Matrix and the title role in John Wick.

people.name: Judi Dench
people.clue: English actor who played M in seven James Bond films and won an Oscar for eight minutes on screen.

people.name: Martin Scorsese
people.clue: American director of Goodfellas and Taxi Driver, who won Best Director for The Departed.

people.name: Scarlett Johansson
people.clue: American actor who played Black Widow in the Marvel films and starred in Lost in Translation.

people.name: Emma Watson
people.clue: English actor who played Hermione Granger and later campaigned for gender equality at the UN.

people.name: Pelé
people.clue: Brazilian footballer who won three World Cups and scored over a thousand career goals.

people.name: Muhammad Ali
people.clue: American boxer who promised to float like a butterfly and sting like a bee, and won the Rumble in the Jungle.

people.name: Serena Williams
people.clue: American tennis player with 23 Grand Slam singles titles, who won one while pregnant.

people.name: Michael Jordan
people.clue: American basketball player who won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls wearing number 23.

people.name: Usain Bolt
people.clue: Jamaican sprinter who holds the 100m and 200m world records and celebrated with a lightning-bolt pose.

people.name: Lionel Messi
people.clue: Argentine footballer with eight Ballons d'Or who finally lifted the World Cup in 2022.

people.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
people.clue: Portuguese footballer and the all-time leading scorer in men's international football.

people.name: Roger Federer
people.clue: Swiss tennis player with 20 Grand Slam titles, known for an elegant one-handed backhand.

people.name: Rafael Nadal
people.clue: Spanish tennis player called the King of Clay, who won the French Open fourteen times.

people.name: Simone Biles
people.clue: American gymnast with more world championship medals than anyone, with several skills named after her.

people.name: Tiger Woods
people.clue: American golfer who won the Masters five times, the first at 21.

people.name: Diego Maradona
people.clue: Argentine footballer who scored both the Hand of God and the Goal of the Century in the same 1986 match.

people.name: Lewis Hamilton
people.clue: British racing driver with seven Formula One world titles and the most career pole positions.

people.name: Michael Phelps
people.clue: American swimmer and the most decorated Olympian ever, with 23 gold medals.

people.name: Magnus Carlsen
people.clue: Norwegian chess grandmaster who became world champion in 2013 and holds the highest rating ever recorded.

people.name: Babe Ruth
people.clue: American baseball player nicknamed the Sultan of Swat, who moved from the Red Sox to the Yankees.

people.name: Wayne Gretzky
people.clue: Canadian ice hockey player known simply as The Great One, whose number 99 is retired league-wide.

people.name: Katie Ledecky
people.clue: American swimmer who dominates long-distance freestyle and first won Olympic gold at 15.

people.name: Albert Einstein
people.clue: German-born physicist who published the theory of relativity and won a Nobel Prize for the photoelectric effect.

people.name: Marie Curie
people.clue: Polish-French physicist and chemist, the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, for work on radioactivity.

people.name: Isaac Newton
people.clue: English mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation, and co-invented calculus.

people.name: Charles Darwin
people.clue: English naturalist who sailed on the Beagle and published On the Origin of Species.

people.name: Stephen Hawking
people.clue: English physicist who studied black holes and wrote A Brief History of Time while living with motor neurone disease.

people.name: Nikola Tesla
people.clue: Serbian-American inventor who championed alternating current against Edison's direct current.

people.name: Ada Lovelace
people.clue: English mathematician who wrote what is considered the first computer algorithm, for Babbage's Analytical Engine.

people.name: Alan Turing
people.clue: English mathematician who helped break the Enigma cipher and devised a famous test for machine intelligence.

people.name: Galileo Galilei
people.clue: Italian astronomer who improved the telescope, found Jupiter's four largest moons, and was tried for heresy.

people.name: Rosalind Franklin
people.clue: English chemist whose X-ray image, Photo 51, was critical to working out the structure of DNA.

people.name: Louis Pasteur
people.clue: French chemist who developed germ theory, a rabies vaccine, and the heat treatment named after him.

people.name: Niels Bohr
people.clue: Danish physicist who modelled the atom with electrons in fixed orbits and shaped quantum theory.

people.name: Gregor Mendel
people.clue: Moravian friar whose experiments with pea plants founded the study of genetics.

people.name: Dmitri Mendeleev
people.clue: Russian chemist who arranged the periodic table and left gaps for elements not yet discovered.

people.name: Jane Goodall
people.clue: English primatologist whose decades of work at Gombe showed that chimpanzees make and use tools.

people.name: Katherine Johnson
people.clue: American mathematician whose orbital calculations sent astronauts to the Moon, later portrayed in Hidden Figures.

people.name: Carl Linnaeus
people.clue: Swedish botanist who invented the two-part Latin naming system for living things.

people.name: Tim Berners-Lee
people.clue: English computer scientist who invented the World Wide Web at CERN and gave it away for free.

people.name: Nelson Mandela
people.clue: Spent 27 years in prison before becoming the first Black president of South Africa.

people.name: Cleopatra
people.clue: The last active pharaoh of Egypt, allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.

people.name: Julius Caesar
people.clue: Roman general who crossed the Rubicon and was assassinated on the Ides of March.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.clue: Led India to independence through nonviolent resistance, including the Salt March.

people.name: Winston Churchill
people.clue: British prime minister through most of the Second World War, who promised blood, toil, tears and sweat.

people.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
people.clue: French general who crowned himself emperor and was finally defeated at Waterloo.

people.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
people.clue: American civil rights leader who delivered the I Have a Dream speech in Washington in 1963.

people.name: Abraham Lincoln
people.clue: US president during the Civil War who issued the Emancipation Proclamation and was assassinated in a theatre.

people.name: Queen Elizabeth II
people.clue: The longest-reigning British monarch, on the throne for seventy years.

people.name: Genghis Khan
people.clue: Founded the Mongol Empire, which became the largest contiguous land empire in history.

people.name: Joan of Arc
people.clue: French teenager who led armies during the Hundred Years War and was burned at the stake in 1431.

people.name: Leonardo da Vinci
people.clue: Italian Renaissance polymath who painted the Mona Lisa and filled notebooks with flying machines.

people.name: Rosa Parks
people.clue: American woman whose refusal to give up a bus seat in Montgomery sparked a year-long boycott.

people.name: Alexander the Great
people.clue: Macedonian king who conquered from Greece to India before dying at 32.

people.name: Catherine the Great
people.clue: Longest-ruling female leader of Russia, who expanded the empire and corresponded with Enlightenment thinkers.

people.name: Christopher Columbus
people.clue: Italian navigator whose 1492 voyage for Spain reached the Americas.

people.name: Anne Frank
people.clue: Teenager who hid in an Amsterdam annexe during the Second World War and left behind a diary.

people.name: Malala Yousafzai
people.clue: Pakistani activist shot for campaigning for girls' education, and the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
